gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 identifies that the example establishes the KL condition only on feasible x in [1,2], while the formal assumption quantifies over all x in an open Omega, including points outside dom p where the level set becomes the entire suboptimal set and the global KL condition fails. Its repair directly corrects the scope claim or restricts the assumption with the associated proof consequences.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the mismatch between the claimed local KL coverage of the motivating constrained example and the Omega-wide formal assumption, including the outside-domain points that force an unsupported global-in-y requirement.

component_coverage.gold_component: The motivating example satisfies the KL inequality only for feasible x in [1,2], not the stated Omega-wide assumption; outside dom p, the convention makes the level set unrestricted and the claimed KL condition fails.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly derives the outside-dom p level-set behavior, gives the failing y=pi consequence, distinguishes the feasible local condition from the formal Omega-wide condition, and proposes a repair addressing that exact scope mismatch.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 concerns unproved closedness of dom p and dom q in limit arguments for Lemma 4 and Lemma 6. Gold I004 instead concerns applying a stationarity definition restricted to locally Lipschitz real-valued functions to the proper closed extended-real-valued objective Psi. The domain-closedness diagnosis and repair do not recognize the missing or mismatched stationarity definition.

ISSUE-003 diagnoses missing closedness of the domains and invalid limit-point arguments in the growth and openness proofs. Gold I005 concerns the absent subdifferential sum-rule justification for the identity partial Psi=partial F*+partial p and the resulting bounded-subgradient closedness argument. These are distinct proof obligations and formulas; adding domain-closedness does not establish the sum rule.
